themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 8 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 6,300% increase (z-score: 23.81)—suggesting either a coordinated campaign or sudden enforcement gap in Midwood/Ocean Parkway this week.
evidence: 8 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (6,300% spike)
Z-score of 23.81 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
Signal appeared in most recent data collection, suggesting emergence within last 7 days
reporting_angles: Investigate whether this reflects a single organized posting campaign (political, commercial, or otherwise) or deterioration in 311 response/enforcement
Street-level reporting: photograph clusters of illegal postings to identify patterns (type, location, advertiser) and interview residents about visual blight impact

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge This Week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints reached 11 this week, a 300% spike above the 2.8 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 4.16), indicating a concentrated burst of vandalism in the district this week.
evidence: 11 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% increase)
Z-score of 4.16 confirms statistically significant spike
Coincides temporally with illegal posting spike, suggesting possible related disorder event or gang activity
reporting_angles: Canvass Midwood/Ocean Parkway blocks to map graffiti hotspots and identify any tags or symbols suggesting crew activity or territorial claims
Interview NYPD and Parks Enforcement to understand response timeline and any pattern recognition (gang markers, protest messaging, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Construction Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints jumped to 47 last week, a 245% increase over the 13.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.87), coinciding with 312 DOB permit filings (236 alterations) and five active rezoning applications that may be triggering noise, obstruction, and disruption.
evidence: 47 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 13.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (245% spike, z-score: 7.87)
312 DOB permit filings in last 90 days with 236 alteration permits suggest sustained construction activity
Five active ULURP/rezoning applications (Ditmas Park West, Beverley Square West, Coney Island Ave, Nostrand Ave, Flatbush Ave) may be generating compliance and neighborhood disruption
reporting_angles: Cross-reference spike in construction complaints with DOB permit timeline; identify which projects are active now and whether they comply with noise/hour restrictions
Interview residents in blocks with highest complaint density about construction impact on sleep, schools, and street safety

themes_detail.label: Obstruction & Street Encroachment Rise
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints spiked to 14 two weeks ago, a 239% increase over the 4.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.24), and concurrent with a 1,100% surge in encampment complaints (6 last week vs. 0.5 baseline), suggesting emerging homelessness or storage/debris blocking public space in Midwood.
evidence: 14 obstruction complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.1 weekly average (239% spike, z-score: 7.24)
6 encampment complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (1,100% spike, z-score: 4.16)
Dual spike suggests both temporary obstructions (debris, parked vehicles, construction materials) and unhoused persons establishing presence in district
reporting_angles: Identify specific blocks or transit nodes where obstructions and encampments are concentrated; determine whether they are near transit, parks, or social services
Interview street-level outreach workers, Parks Enforcement, and NYPD to understand whether this is new or enforced away cyclically; assess if services/shelters are capacity-constrained

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Sustained Rise
themes_detail.summary: Street/sidewalk noise complaints peaked at 81 two weeks ago, a 288% increase over the 20.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.21), and residential noise remains elevated at 1,992 complaints over 90 days, indicating chronic noise stress compounded by a recent event or construction surge.
evidence: 81 street/sidewalk noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 20.9 weekly average (288% spike, z-score: 4.21)
1,992 residential noise complaints over 90 days—highest category after heat/hot water—showing chronic baseline
Spike timing correlates with construction complaint surge, suggesting possible event-driven or project-related noise (demolition, heavy machinery, late-hour work)
reporting_angles: Audit 311 noise complaint data for time-of-day patterns; identify whether complaints cluster during construction hours or late night (possible code violations)
Interview residents in high-complaint blocks about source of noise (construction, bars/restaurants, traffic, vehicle alarms) and impact on sleep and children's schooling
